steps.title: Definition
steps.body: A review evaluates a product, service, or creative work, providing a judgment supported by evidence to help readers make informed decisions.

steps.title: Include
steps.body: Title and type of work/product Key details (author, director, release date) A brief overview of what it's about An engaging hook to interest readers

steps.title: Key Elements
steps.body: Discuss specific aspects (acting, directing, plot, etc.) Use examples to illustrate your points Balance positive and negative aspects Use new paragraphs for different aspects

steps.title: Include
steps.body: Clear overall judgment Who would enjoy this Star rating or recommendation Final memorable comment

steps.title: Try it yourself
steps.body: What are the four key elements of an effective review? | Why should you avoid major spoilers in a film or book review? | Write an introduction for a review of a restaurant you've visited.

steps.title: Check your answers
steps.body: Judgment (your opinion), Evidence (specific examples), Balanced view (pros and cons), Recommendation (who should see/read/use it). | Spoilers ruin the experience for readers who haven't seen the film or read the book. You want to inform their decision, not reveal the ending. | Your introduction should include: the restaurant name, location/cuisine type, and an engaging hook that hints at your overall judgment.

steps.title: Exam tips
steps.body: Start with a hook that engages your reader State your judgment clearly and early Support every opinion with specific examples Balance positive and negative points Avoid major spoilers in film and book reviews End with a clear recommendation Consider a star rating or similar summary
